title: Close a half-full gallon paint can: steady the can and tap the set-on lid down all the way round with a rubber mallet
context: Closing a part-used can of paint so it does not skin over is routine for painters (about 370,000 in the US), general maintenance and repair workers (about 1.5 million) and construction laborers, and a common household job. A ring-and-plug lid is set on square and tapped down with a rubber mallet all the way round its rim until every part of it is seated flush in the can's groove, while the other hand steadies the can on its drop cloth.
setup: Bench top is z = 0.7475 m; everything is real size. A folded cotton canvas drop cloth (620 x 500 x 4 mm, off-white with old paint spots, near edge folded over) lies on the bench centred at x 0.37, y -0.02. On it stands a 1 US gallon (3.78 L) open-top steel paint can (168 mm across the chimes, 190 mm tall, tinplate, ring-and-plug top, wire bail with a black plastic grip lying down on the far side, printed paper label of a made-up maker, 'Harbor Blue' interior latex, paint run down the wall and wet in the ring's groove), about half full, 2.4 kg, its axis at x 0.37, y 0.05. Its tinplate plug lid (157 mm across the curl, 8 mm plug, 70 g, tint-recipe sticker on top) is set on the ring but not tapped down: 4 mm proud of seated. An 8 oz black rubber mallet (head 51 mm across x 92 mm long, wooden handle 25 mm thick, 305 mm overall, 0.31 kg) lies on the cloth, its head's centre at x 0.40, y -0.24 and its handle running back toward the arms and left (heading 120 degrees).
scoring: The lid's rim is 8 sectors of 45 degrees round the can's axis; a sector is seated by a tap: the mallet's lower face coming down on it (face centre 40-95 mm from the axis, within 4 mm of the lid's top, at 0.04 m/s or more, within 25 degrees of flat). 0.25: at least 3 sectors seated. 0.5: at least 6. 0.75: all 8 and the lid down within 1 mm of seated (flush in the ring). 1.0: also the mallet laid back on the cloth at rest (head centre under 60 mm up, under 0.02 m/s and 0.2 rad/s) and every finger pad at least 50 mm from the mallet, the can and the lid, held 1 s. The can pushed more than 15 mm or tipped more than 8 degrees at any time caps the score at 0.5; the mallet off the bench or the can knocked over scores 0. Stages latch once reached.
reset_notes: Fixed poses, no randomisation: the lid set on the can 4 mm proud, the mallet on the cloth beside it; the arms at their rest poses.
fidelity: PhysX 240 Hz, real-size parts: detailed visual meshes over simple hidden colliders; the label is a printed image of a made-up maker. Paint is not simulated (static surfaces only). The can is one rigid body with its contents' mass, centre of mass low. The plug lid is a vertical slide on the can (the ring holds it sideways), stopped 4 mm proud; its seal is a rule: once all 8 sectors are tapped the stop drops 4 mm and the lid falls flush. No dents.
